extracted.intended_audience: Personnel assigned or preparing to serve as Public Information Officer (PIO); Assistant PIOs; Incident Management Team members; public- or private-sector responders operating within ICS environments
extracted.subtask_description: A four-day training course preparing personnel to serve as a Public Information Officer on an Incident Management Team, teaching incident communications, media relations, information management, and coordination with Command Staff and partner agencies. Emphasizes scenario-based exercises, media briefings, and practical application of PIO duties across incident phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary PIO duties — point of contact and information coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer (PIO) serves as the primary point of contact between the Incident Management Team and the public, media, and partner agencies, ensuring timely, accurate, and coordinated information throughout incident operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO is a Command Staff role responsible for managing communications and supporting situational awareness across incident operations; implies emphasis on timeliness, accuracy, and coordination when producing public information (e.g., press releases, briefings, partner notifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain PIO role and importance during incident operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the role and importance of the Public Information Officer during incident operations, including initial response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the PIO's mission across phases (initial response through demobilization) is a learning objective used to assess knowledge of the position and its operational significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information management fundamentals and establishing PIO staff/workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the fundamentals of information management and how to establish the PIO staff and workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers organization of information flows, documentation, recordkeeping, and logistics for a PIO unit (staffing, physical/virtual workspace). Assessment may include setting up a functional PIO workspace in exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop communications strategy and media plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an effective communications strategy and media plan for sharing incident information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on planning: target audiences, messaging, channels (including press releases and social media), timing, and coordination with Command Staff and partner agencies. Demonstrations or written plans may be used as evaluation artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations best practices, including social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate best practices for media relations, including social media engagement and problem-solving during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical skills such as conducting media briefings, crafting statements, engaging on social platforms, and resolving media-related issues are taught and evaluated via role-play, briefings, and scenario work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of Assistant Public Information Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the roles and responsibilities of Assistant Public Information Officers and their relationship to the PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies delegation, supervision, and coordination within the PIO team; may be assessed by assigning assistant roles in exercises and evaluating teamwork and role clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building and maintaining relationships with IMT and participation in briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how to build and maintain effective relationships with the Incident Management Team and participate in meetings and briefings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on integration into Command Staff, information-sharing protocols, and contributions to briefings; evaluation via observed participation and quality of liaison activities during exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing and maintaining community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe steps for establishing and maintaining community relations during an incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers outreach strategies, stakeholder engagement, and community trust-building; may include scenario tasks such as stakeholder messaging or community briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing special situations involving public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply appropriate actions for managing special situations involving public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes handling sensitive information, rumors/misinformation, controversies, and evolving incidents; assessed through problem-solving exercises and simulated special-case incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety considerations for PIOs and escorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe safety considerations for PIOs and those they escort or work with in the incident environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses personal safety, situational awareness for PIOs in the field, and protocols when escorting media or other personnel; evaluation may include scenario safety planning and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO responsibilities during transition and demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline the PIO’s responsibilities during incident transition and demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers handover of information, final communications, documentation, and after-action messaging; assessed by evaluating completeness of transition plans and demobilization communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate PIO effectiveness and apply lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PIO effectiveness and apply lessons learned through exercise components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course includes exercises with after-action review elements to measure performance, identify gaps, and apply improvements; assessment includes participation in evaluations and documented lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and evaluation methods (scenario-based, role-play, briefings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities may include instructor-led, in-person training supported by realistic scenario-based learning, group discussion and facilitated instruction, media briefings and role-play exercises, incident communication planning activities, problem-solving exercises, and asynchronous activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the course uses experiential methods to teach and assess skills—expect practical evaluation through role-plays, simulated briefings, planning tasks, and facilitated debriefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course length and contact hours
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for planning and scheduling; sets expectation for contact time and depth of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended prerequisite — ICS-300
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended Pre-requisite: Successful completion of ICS-300 (please check with your organization or Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to determine whether EMSI recommended pre-requisite completion is required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates recommended baseline ICS knowledge for participants; may be enforced by organizations as an enrollment requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment note — FEMA course equivalency and certification status
rubrics_metrics.description: This course aligns with FEMA’s National Preparedness Course Catalog for the NIMS ICS All-Hazards Public Information Officer (0952) but is not an official FEMA course and does not confer FEMA certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies equivalence to FEMA learning objectives but warns participants that completion does not produce FEMA certification—important for credential expectations and organizational approval.
